title: Thyagarajan Takes 11 Wickets As Hyderabad Beat Andhra By 267 Runs
excerpt: Himateja's unbeaten 123 rescues Hyderabad's second innings before Thyagarajan's 6 for 35 bowls Andhra out for 130 in Mulapadu
body:
• Hyderabad beat Andhra by 267 runs in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group B match in Mulapadu, bowling Andhra out for 130 in pursuit of 398.
  • Tanay Thyagarajan took 11 wickets in the match — 5 for 63 and 6 for 35 — and added an unbeaten 53, winning Player of the Match for the second game running.
  • Kodimela Himateja made an unbeaten 123 off 202 balls to rescue Hyderabad from 101 for 5 in their second innings and set up the declaration at 306 for 7.
  • The result was Hyderabad's second outright win in two matches, following their innings victory over Tripura in the opener.

Hyderabad completed a 267-run win over Andhra in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group B match at Mulapadu on Wednesday, with left-arm spinner Tanay Thyagarajan finishing with 11 wickets in the match. Set 398 to win, Andhra were bowled out for 130 in 30.5 overs on the final day, Thyagarajan taking 6 for 35 in 11 overs to add to his 5 for 63 in the first innings, according to the match reports on Cricbuzz and Cricketnmore.

A first-innings lead built with bat and ball

Hyderabad, who won the toss and chose to bat, were bowled out for 275 in 86 overs in their first innings. The openers put on 109 for the first wicket, Abhirath Reddy made 67 off 108 balls, Rahul Radesh finished unbeaten on 58 off 105 balls, Tanmay Agarwal added 42 and Pragnay Reddy 31. For Andhra, Tripurana Vijay took 4 for 90, Lalith Mohan 3 for 78 and Saurabh Kumar 3 for 75, as recorded in the full scorecard on CricTracker.

Andhra replied with 184 in 63 overs. Mohammed Siraj gave Hyderabad an early breakthrough, and Thyagarajan then worked through the innings as Andhra slid from 91 for 3 to 149 for 7. Shaik Rasheed made 61, the only sustained resistance, while Thyagarajan took 5 for 63 — his second successive five-wicket haul of the season — and G. Aniketh Reddy took 2 for 60. Hyderabad led by 91 runs.

Himateja turns a collapse into a declaration

Hyderabad resumed the third day on 78 for 1 in their second innings and slipped to 101 for 5 in the morning session. Kodimela Himateja rebuilt the innings, adding 99 with Ruthik Mende, who made 31, and then 93 with Thyagarajan, who hit an unbeaten 53 off 64 balls. Himateja finished on 123 not out off 202 balls, with 10 fours and five sixes, and Hyderabad, captained by Siraj, declared on 306 for 7 in 95.3 overs. Kavuri Saiteja took 4 for 40 for Andhra. The declaration left Andhra needing 398, and they closed the third day on 7 for 2.

Thyagarajan finishes the job on the final morning

Andhra's chase never recovered. They were 98 for 7 during the final morning, and although captain Ricky Bhui made 26, K. V. Sasikanth 23 and Lalith Mohan 17, no batter stayed long enough to threaten the target. Thyagarajan struck twice in quick succession and finished with 6 for 35, while Aniketh Reddy took 3 for 57. Andhra were all out for 130, and Thyagarajan was named Player of the Match for the second game running, after also winning the award against Tripura last week.

What the result means

The win gives Hyderabad a second outright victory in as many matches, after their innings-and-40-run victory over Tripura in the opening round. Reports from the ground said the six points took Hyderabad to the top of the Group B table with 13 points. Andhra, who had drawn their first match against Karnataka, suffered their first defeat of the season. For Hyderabad, the pattern of the first two rounds has been clear: a spinner controlling both innings, and a middle-order batter converting pressure into a match-defining score when the top order faltered.

For Andhra, the match turned on two passages — the slide from 91 for 3 to 149 for 7 in the first innings, and the loss of five wickets for barely 20 runs at the start of the second innings, from 78 for 1 overnight to 101 for 5. Rasheed's 61 and Vijay's 4 for 90 in the first innings showed Andhra could compete for periods, but they could not sustain that pressure across four days against Thyagarajan, who scored runs as well as taking wickets in both innings.
